subject: Model mix & pricing follow-up: token volumes and unit economics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightlayer.com>, Sara Ahmed <sara.ahmed@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: model mix, token volumes, next steps

Hi Jordan / Sara —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a scoped pricing + recommendation: 

Recap of what we heard in the call:
- Primary use: customer support chatbot (chat completions) + semantic search for KB (embeddings) + a small rerank pipeline for results quality.
- Latency target: 300–500ms p50 for chat, embeddings can be batch/async.
- Privacy: data scope is non-PII for now but may include customer identifiers later — you flagged potential interest in Private deployment after we show costs.

Asks / what we need from you to finalize an estimate:
1) Confirm expected monthly token volumes (baseline and peak). If helpful, a 3‑month projection or steady-state monthly is fine.
2) Confirm tentative model mix (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) as a percent split of total tokens. We heard a rough split on the call but want to lock it for unit economics.
3) Target unit economics: is there a target $/1M tokens you’re trying to hit (ballpark range is fine).

Based on our initial notes, please send any forecast you have — even a single row with "expected monthly tokens" and "peak TPS" will do. I attached the mutual action plan and a blank token forecast spreadsheet to make this quick.

Next steps I suggest: once we get the volume/mix and target $/1M, Neha and I will produce two concrete options:
- Hosted (fast to market) — per-model unit pricing, predictable SLA, scaling.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) — lower unit cost at commit, includes autoscaling/bursting options.

Thanks — available tomorrow 10–11am PT for a quick follow if you prefer to walk through the numbers live.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: BL-token-forecast.xlsx (blank forecast)

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model mix, token volumes, next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Per your asks, here are the numbers we have so far (internal forecast, high level):

- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~150,000,000 tokens/month (150M)
- Peak day: ~8M tokens/day (anticipated during product launch windows)
- Preliminary model mix (by token share): Chat completions: 60% (~90M tokens/mo), Embeddings: 30% (~45M), Rerank: 10% (~15M)
- Target unit economics: aiming for around $250–$350 per 1M tokens as a blended goal. We understand hosted will be higher; interested in how much Dedicated would lower this.

Notes / questions:
- For embeddings we expect a mixture of streaming (online) and periodic batch re-indexing; some peak jobs could spike embedding usage.
- Latency is more critical for chat; embeddings can tolerate longer tail.
- We’d like to understand quantization/precision options (FP16 vs int8/4) and impact on quality.

I attached our internal forecast export (BL-token-forecast.xlsx) with monthly buckets — let me know if you want it in a different format. Procurement will likely engage in mid‑July; target contract start late July/early August.

Would love a short call with Neha/Dev to validate technical assumptions and pricing bands tomorrow if that works.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightLayer Systems
jordan.lee@brightlayer.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@brightlayer.com>, Sara Ahmed <sara.ahmed@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model mix, token volumes, next steps

Jordan — great, thanks for the detail and the spreadsheet. Based on the 150M/mo baseline and the 60/30/10 model mix you gave, here are two preliminary, high-level pricing bands (blended $/1M tokens) to set expectations. These are estimates — Neha will validate quality tradeoffs and Dev will confirm latency/capacity specifics in the follow-up call.

Option A — Hosted (no commit):
- Chat completions (60%): ~$420–$520 per 1M tokens
- Embeddings (30%): ~$80–$140 per 1M tokens (varies by embedding model and batch size)
- Rerank (10%): ~$250–$350 per 1M tokens
- Blended: ~ $340–$410 per 1M tokens (weighted by your mix)

Option B — Dedicated (1yr reserved capacity, 3–6 week lead time to provision):
- Chat completions (60%): ~$220–$300 per 1M tokens
- Embeddings (30%): ~$45–$85 per 1M tokens
- Rerank (10%): ~$120–$200 per 1M tokens
- Blended: ~ $180–$240 per 1M tokens (assuming 1yr commit / predictable traffic)

Key assumptions behind the bands:
- Chat numbers assume a moderately optimized model variant (quantized int8) with continuous batching and prefix caching for sessioned chat. Lower-latency/ higher-accuracy variants will push the hosted ranges up.
- Embeddings price range depends heavily on batch size and offline vs online workflows; bulk re-indexing can be ramped into lower-cost batch windows.
- Rerank is compute-heavy relative to tokens; if rerank runs as a small model before full generation we can drop cost with a lightweight candidate re-scoring model.

Next suggested steps:
1) Quick technical sync (30m) with Dev + Neha to validate latency and quantization tolerances — propose Thu 9:30am PT or Fri 10:00am PT.
2) If numbers look good, we will convert Option B into a draft MSA/term sheet and a sample capacity commit worksheet for procurement.

If your blended target is $250–$350 per 1M tokens, Dedicated gets you comfortably into that range; Hosted gets you closer at the top end of your target. We’ll fill in exact line items once we pick models and commit levels.

Would you like me to prepare a side-by-side hosted vs dedicated cost model using your attached forecast? I can have that ready by end of day tomorrow if you confirm the call.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
